verdict.rationale: The Trusted Agent Protocol lets a merchant cryptographically identify the specific agent behind each browsing or payment interaction. It uses RFC 9421 signatures with agent-browser-auth or agent-payer-auth tags, checked against Visa public keys and an agent-registry reference implementation. Agent-specific payment tokens and captured commerce signals tie each authorized purchase to the user's instruction. That gives a merchant the raw material to attribute orders, but attribution would have to be built by the merchant at checkout. Missing for 10: any documented order or transaction attribution field identifying the originating agent, merchant reporting, dashboard or API filtering of transactions by agent, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
